flagged.evidence: Step 1.1 says time reversal “preserves all hypotheses,” and the Remarks specify replacing N by -N. But def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects says this reverses future/past labels, while def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry requires the second fundamental form with respect to the future unit normal to equal the fixed K; reversing N alone reverses that normal and changes the induced second fundamental form to -K. Also, def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model clause (a) requires g(n,N)<0, and def-gr-dust-matter-model clause (a) requires g(u,N)<0. With those fixed matter fields unchanged, replacing N by -N makes the pairings positive. Thus the reversed tuples need not be developments of the same fixed data/model, and no time-reversal covariance or transformed-data hypothesis licenses reducing the past-only case to the future-only argument.
